{
  "title": "The Keeper of the Decades",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The dust motes dance in a shaft of amber light, settling on leather spines and yellowed paper.",
  "question": "Who is the traveler who returns every decade, carrying a book that never feels new?",
  "journey": "First, it was a boy in a heavy wool coat, his boots leaving wet slush on the mahogany floor. Ten years passed, and the same coat appeared, the same boots, but the boy’s face remained a frozen portrait of childhood. Then came the frost of a second decade. The library doors creaked open to the same silhouette, a steady rhythm of footsteps against the silence. He never spoke, only placed the volume on the desk with a soft, heavy thud.",
  "discovery": "The librarian opened the book to the middle page. There, in the margin, was a handwritten note: 'The garden is blooming.' It was the same note, written in the same elegant ink, appearing every ten years as if the time between arrivals didn't exist for him.",
  "emotional_turn": "The librarian touched the paper, feeling the ghost of a pulse in the grain. He realized the book wasn't being borrowed; it was being held in trust, a bridge across a century of solitude.",
  "payoff": "One evening, the man finally sat down. He didn't leave. He opened the book to the final page and began to write a new note, his hand trembling with the weight of a thousand years.",
  "after_image": "The lamp flickers once, and the chair remains occupied by a shadow of old memories.",
  "hero_shot": "A single white glove resting on a table, holding a pen that has run dry of ink."
}
